<h2 style="text-align: left;"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Shredded Buffalo Chicken</span></strong></h2>
<h3><em>What kind of chicken to use?</em></h3>
<p>I typically use <strong>leftover rotisserie chicken</strong>, just because that’s usually what I’ve got on hand. However, you can definitely cook up some fresh chicken and use that instead if you’d prefer. In both cases, I recommend <strong>shredding the chicken</strong>, as opposed to dicing it. That way it’s more likely to stay intact in the wrap and it soaks up the sauce a little easier.</p>
<h3><em>What kind of sauce to use?</em></h3>
<p>For this recipe, I do use a <a href="https://www.dontgobaconmyheart.co.uk/homemade-buffalo-sauce/">homemade buffalo sauce</a>, but feel free to use store-bought if that is more convenient for you. In such case, I recommend <strong>Franks Red Hot Buffalo Wings Sauce. </strong>Just definitely make sure it’s not regular hot sauce, otherwise, your mouth will be in flames!</p>

<div id="AdThrive_Content_1_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h2 style="text-align: left;"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Buffalo Chicken Wraps</span></strong></h2>
<p>I love a <strong>lettuce</strong>, <strong>cabbage</strong> and <strong>carrot</strong> combo. I think it really works, especially in the context of buffalo chicken. It offers the perfect amount of <strong>colour</strong>, <strong>crunch</strong> and <strong>flavour</strong> whilst still allowing the chicken to champion the wrap.</p>
<p>I find things such as tomatoes and cucumber a little distracting. Plus they’ve got pretty high water contents, which alongside the buffalo chicken and blue cheese sauce could turn things a little sloppy!</p>
<p>But either way, stick with a flour tortilla and keep the salad:chicken ratio under control and you’ll be fine.</p>

<h2><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Buffalo Chicken Wraps FAQ</strong></span></h2>
<h3><em>Do I serve these hot or cold?</em></h3>
<p>I recommend cold. You could warm them up by toasting them in a dry pan, or, heating the buffalo sauce before mixing it with the chicken and heating the wraps. However the steam softens the veg pretty quickly, so they tend to be a tad sloppy.</p>
<h3><em>What else could I add to these wraps?</em></h3>
<p>These wraps are awesome as they are, but you could consider the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cheese (Monterey Jack works great)</li>
<li>Bacon</li>
<li>Spring Onion</li>
<li>Celery</li>
<li>Avocado</li>
</ul>
<p>As I mentioned, I’d steer away from things such as cucumber and tomato, otherwise, the wraps end up on the soggier side!</p>
<h3><em>Can I make buffalo chicken wraps ahead of time?</em></h3>
<p>Personally, I like making wraps fresh. Especially these as they are quite saucy (buffalo sauce/blue cheese sauce) the veg & wrap tends to go soggy if made in advance. If you want to get ahead of the game you can still make the blue cheese sauce and combine chicken with buffalo sauce and cover/store overnight in the fridge.</p>

<p>Once you’ve tightly wrapped them, just slice them in half and tuck right in!</p>

	<div id="recipe-4787-notes" class="wprm-recipe-notes-container wprm-block-text-normal"><div id="AdThrive_Recipe_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-recipe adthrive-recipe-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3 class="wprm-recipe-header wprm-recipe-notes-header wprm-block-text-none wprm-align-left wprm-header-decoration-none" style="">Notes</h3><div class="wprm-recipe-notes"><span style="display: block;"><strong>a</strong><strong>) How to make Shredded Chicken </strong>- If you aren't using rotisserie chicken and only have raw breasts, have no fear. Here's how I make my own juicy shredded chicken: </span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;">- Season both sides of 2 chicken breasts with salt and pepper.<br>- Heat a little oil in a deep pan, fry each side of the chicken on high just to get some colour.<br>- Pour in enough water (or chicken stock) to cover the chicken, place a lid on top and poach on a simmer until the centre is no longer pink. The chicken temp should reach 165f/74c on a thermometer. Depending on size this should take between 8-12 minutes.<br>- Place in a bowl and with two forks, shred to desired texture.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>b) Buffalo Sauce - </strong>Most supermarkets/grocery stores will sell Original Buffalo Sauce so feel free to use that if you aren't keen on making <a href="https://www.dontgobaconmyheart.co.uk/homemade-buffalo-sauce/">Homemade Buffalo Sauce</a>.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>c) Blue Cheese Sauce</strong> - You can use my <a href="https://www.dontgobaconmyheart.co.uk/homemade-blue-cheese-dip/">Homemade Blue Cheese Dip</a> or pick up some store bought blue cheese sauce (usually in the salad dressing/sauce section). If you're not keen on blue cheese you can sub <a href="https://www.dontgobaconmyheart.co.uk/homemade-ranch/">Ranch</a>!</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>d) Sauciness - </strong>Personally I love my wraps drowned in both buffalo and blue cheese Sauce. However, to control the sauce content simply add the buffalo sauce little by little into the chicken and stop at desired texture. It's much easier to add more than take it out! At the same time feel free to alter the amount of blue cheese sauce too.</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>e) Additions</strong> - These are awesome as they are, but here's some ideas for additions if you fancy something a little extra:</span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<ul>
<li>Cheese (Monterey Jack works great)</li>
<li>Bacon</li>
<li>Spring Onion</li>
<li>Celery</li>
<li>Avocado</li>
</ul>
<span style="display: block;"><strong>f) Calories</strong> - per wrap assuming all the sauce is used and shared between 4.</span></div></div>
